chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu al-Qasim al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Isma'il ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام), who said:
When death came upon Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام), before that he brought out a basket or a box that was with him and said: “O Muhammad, carry this box.”
He said: So it was carried by four men. Then when he passed away, his brothers came claiming what was in the box, and they said: “Give us our share in the box.”

So he said: “By Allah, you have no share in it; and if you had any share in it, he would not have handed it over to me.” And in the box were the weapons of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and his books.

key_terms.الْوَفَاةُ: death; the approach of a person's passing
key_terms.سَفَطًا: a basket or casket used for keeping valuable items
key_terms.صُنْدُوقًا: a box or chest containing entrusted items
key_terms.كُتُبُهُ: his books; written materials belonging to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)
key_terms.نَصِيبَنَا: our share; a claimed portion or entitlement

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the designation of Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) through the entrusted box of the Prophet’s آثار?
ai.summary: This narration describes how Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام), near the time of his death, entrusted a box to Muhammad, later identified as Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام). After his passing, others from the family claimed a right to its contents, but Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) clarified that its transfer to him signified exclusive designation. The box contained the weapons of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and his books, indicating inherited religious authority.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Abu Al Qasim Al Kufy, from Muhammad Bin Sahl, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balad, 
(It has been narrated) from Ismail Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, son of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the death presented itself to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, before that, he<sup>asws</sup> brought out a basket or a box which was with him<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>! Carry away this box!’

He (the narrator) said: ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> carried it between four (help of four people). So when he (Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>) passed away, his<sup>asws</sup> brothers came over claiming whatever was in the box, and they said, ‘Give us our share in the box’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! There is no share for you all in it, and had there been a share for you all in it, it would not have been handed over to me<sup>asws</sup>’. And in the box were the weapons of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and his<sup>saww</sup> Books’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from abu al-Qasim al-Kufi from Muhammad ibn Sahl from Ibrahim ibn abu al-Bilad from Isma’il ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.
“When Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) was about to leave this world he took out a basket or a box that was with him. He then said, “O Muhammad take this box. “
The narrator has said that then he (Muhammad) took the box with four people. When The Imam (a.s.) died his sons came asking for the box and said, “Give us our share from the box.”

He (Muhammad) then said to them, “By Allah, there is nothing for you in it. Had there been anything for you he would not have given it to me.” In the box there were the Armament of the Messenger of Allah and his books.”
